::: {#sol-linearity-use}

Pull the constant $1/n$ out and split the sum, both by @thm-linearity-expectation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Ep[\bar X]
&= \Ep\sb{\avgin X_i} \\
&= \avgin \Ep[X_i] \\
&= \frac{1}{n}\,(n\mean) \\
&= \mean
\end{aligned}
$$

So the sample average is right *on average*.
Independence was never used: @thm-linearity-expectation holds regardless,
so this much would be true even for draws that influence one another.

What it does not tell us is how far any *particular* sample average falls
from $\mean$ --- that is a statement about variance, not expectation,
and it is where independence does the work.
The distinction matters because an estimator or fitted model is a function of one
particular sample.
Knowing that the procedure is right on average says nothing about
the estimate actually in front of you,
and separating those two statements is foundational to understanding bias and variance.

:::
